title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Franklin & Marshall traditions, recurring ceremonies, and ceremonial objects that mark the academic year, athletics, finals, and graduation.

cards.title: Begin Together at Convocation
cards.subtitle: F&M’s formal welcome for incoming and transfer students
cards.notes: Check the annual program before attending, then watch how F&M formally opens the academic year by welcoming its newest students.
cards.short_summary: The College community gathers to recognize new students and formally begin another academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: Franklin & Marshall identifies Convocation as a College tradition that gathers the community to celebrate incoming and transfer students and open the academic year.
cards.access_notes: Annual ceremony; consult the current Convocation page for the venue, date, seating, and attendance details.

cards.title: Return for True Blue Weekend
cards.subtitle: Homecoming and Family Weekend in F&M blue
cards.notes: Use the published weekend schedule to choose reunions, campus programs, and family activities appropriate to your connection with F&M.
cards.short_summary: Alumni, families, friends, and the campus community reconnect during F&M’s annual three-day gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: F&M describes True Blue Weekend as its annual Homecoming and Family Weekend, a three-day campus celebration drawing alumni, family, and friends.
cards.access_notes: Programming and eligibility vary by event; consult the annual True Blue Weekend schedule and registration information.

cards.title: Play to Win the Wagon
cards.subtitle: F&M and Dickinson’s football trophy tradition since 1963
cards.notes: Find the annual F&M–Dickinson football date, then look for the miniature Conestoga Wagon trophy tied to a rivalry first played in 1889.
cards.short_summary: The Diplomats and Dickinson Red Devils contest a miniature wagon trophy rooted in the schools’ early football travel.
cards.evidence_claim: F&M states that its football team and Dickinson have competed annually for the Conestoga Wagon Trophy since 1963; the trophy replicates the wagon once used to transport players.
cards.access_notes: Game date, venue, admission, and spectator policies vary; confirm them through the current athletics schedule.

cards.title: Pause Finals at FlapJack Fest
cards.subtitle: A free finals-week meal served by F&M employees
cards.notes: Watch Student Affairs announcements during finals, then bring your student ID if requested and take a real break over the late-semester meal.
cards.short_summary: Faculty and professional staff serve pancakes and other breakfast food as students pause during finals week.
cards.evidence_claim: F&M documents FlapJack Fest as a finals-week study break with free pancakes, eggs, tots, and more, served by faculty and professional staff in the Dining Hall.
cards.access_notes: A finals-week campus meal; verify the current date, serving period, location, and student-access requirements.

cards.title: Step Away at Spring Arts
cards.subtitle: F&M’s spring-semester break for food and music
cards.notes: Follow campus event announcements for the date and location, then set aside classwork long enough to hear the music and join the activities.
cards.short_summary: Students gather during the spring semester for an organized break featuring food, music, and recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: F&M identifies Spring Arts as a spring-semester event where students can step away from classwork, have fun, eat food, and listen to music.
cards.access_notes: Campus event details may change annually; confirm the current schedule, location, and participation rules.

cards.title: Bookend College Under Lux et Lex
cards.subtitle: Students reverse direction beneath F&M’s Light and Law arch
cards.notes: Notice which way the class passes beneath the Klauder-Apple Walkway arch: arrival and graduation send students in opposite directions.
cards.short_summary: The same inscribed arch marks both a student’s entrance to F&M and the closing passage before Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: F&M states that new students walk beneath the Lux et Lex arch to begin their College journey and pass under it in the opposite direction four years later before Commencement.
cards.access_notes: The ceremonial walks are tied to new-student arrival and pre-Commencement programming; consult the applicable schedule.

cards.title: Gather at the Senior Bonfire
cards.subtitle: A class-only farewell hosted by the Senior Class Cabinet
cards.notes: Eligible seniors should follow cabinet announcements, dress for an outdoor evening, and use the gathering to reconnect before Commencement.
cards.short_summary: The graduating class closes its campus chapter together with a bonfire, games, music, s’mores, and a farewell gift.
cards.evidence_claim: F&M documents the Senior Bonfire as an annual event open to the senior class and hosted by the Senior Class Cabinet, with s’mores, music, games, and a farewell gift.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to the senior class; follow official instructions concerning the date, location, weather, and fire-safety controls.

cards.title: Carry Old Main Into Ceremony
cards.subtitle: A tower-shaped mace containing timber from Franklin College’s 1788 quarters
cards.notes: When the mace appears in a formal procession, look for Old Main’s four-spired silhouette and remember the historic oak beam sealed inside.
cards.short_summary: F&M’s ceremonial emblem physically connects modern academic processions to the College’s earliest Lancaster home.
cards.evidence_claim: F&M says its mace replicates Old Main’s four-spired tower, contains part of an oak beam from Franklin College’s 1788 quarters, and has served as an official ceremonial emblem since 1967.
cards.access_notes: A ceremonial object rather than a general-access attraction; it is displayed or carried when College protocol calls for it.

cards.title: Pass the Alumni Torch
cards.subtitle: A renewed Commencement handoff first proposed by the Class of 1904
cards.notes: At Commencement, watch for the replica torch and read its handoff as a welcome that moves graduating students into the alumni community.
cards.short_summary: A replica restored F&M’s literal passing-of-the-torch ceremony after the original vanished in 2000.
cards.evidence_claim: F&M’s Alumni Association says the Class of 1904 created a Commencement torch-passing tradition to welcome graduates as alumni; after the original disappeared in 2000, a replica renewed the tradition.
cards.access_notes: Observed as part of Commencement protocol; ceremony admission and viewing arrangements are published separately each year.

cards.title: Recognize the Williamson Medalist
cards.subtitle: F&M’s annual Commencement honor for character, leadership, and scholarship
cards.notes: Read the annual recipient’s citation before Commencement, then listen for the medal presentation among the College’s formal recognitions.
cards.short_summary: Since 1922, F&M has singled out one graduating senior through its highest student award.
cards.evidence_claim: F&M states that the Williamson Medal is presented annually at Commencement to the graduating-class member with the highest standing in character, leadership, and scholarship, a practice continuing since 1922.
cards.access_notes: The recipient is recognized through annual Commencement programming; consult the current ceremony information for access details.
